target: 1776:8383 (18 · Review), 1084:4527 (11 · Templates), 1776:8373 (07 · Brand) — the six-isolated-modules premise, restated for the design file
claim: EVENT-GRAPH.json reports six fully isolated modules — collaboration, drag, fonts, forms, interactions, templates — which reads as six features with no door.
truth: Only two of the six have no door, and the premise mis-sorts the rest. FORMS: a door exists but not the one the module was built for — a form is configured through Element Properties as raw HTML attributes that really do export, while FormConfig, FormHandler, FormspreeInjector and FormSettingsSection are all unreachable. INTERACTIONS: a full door, mounted; the module is bypassed rather than disconnected, because the inspector writes the same storage slot through ElementOperations instead of InteractionManager. FONTS: genuinely no door — no method on composer.fonts has ever been called in the repo's history. DRAG: a door in one direction only; the canvas calls DragManager four times and reads it back zero times, so the engine mirror is write-only while React state is the real source of truth. TEMPLATES: the engine class has no door and should be deleted, but the FEATURE is one of the most complete in the product — a 718-line panel with apply, progress, replace-confirm, preview, usage and new-page mode. COLLABORATION: not isolated at all; three listeners subscribe with raw string literals that ARE the constants, which is why the scanner missed them. So for the Figma file: two modules need boards drawn (interactions, canvas drop feedback), one needs boards marked (fonts), one needs a board created for a door that exists in an unexpected place (forms), one needs its boards corrected rather than retired (templates), and one needs its premise corrected before anything is marked (collaboration).

target: 1776:8381 (08 · Inspector), 1776:8375 (03 · Layers), 1779:5 (09 · Canvas) — private-bus emitters, for whoever reads FONT_*/TEMPLATE_* as drawable events
claim: events.ts declares FONT_*, TEMPLATE_* and COLLAB_* constants alongside every other event, which reads as one bus whose orphans are all equally fixable.
truth: Three of the six modules emit on a manager's OWN EventEmitter rather than the composer bus, so 22 of the 58 orphans in these six modules can never have a composer listener no matter how well any UI is written. That is a code-shape fact, not a design gap, and it is the reason none of these events will ever drive a board state: FontManager, TemplateManager and CollaborationManager all extend EventEmitter and emit with `this.emit`, while FormHandler, InteractionManager and DragManager use `this.composer.emit`. Composer forwards exactly one private event onward. Recording it so no board is drawn on the assumption that, say, FONT_LOADED could repaint the canvas as things stand.
evidence: Private-bus emitters: FontManager.ts:46, TemplateManager.ts:49, CollaborationManager.ts:55 — all `extends EventEmitter`, all emits are `this.emit`. Shared-bus emitters: FormHandler.ts:125 etc., InteractionManager.ts:51 etc., DragManager.ts:88 etc. The single forward is Composer.ts:352 subscribing `collab.manager.on("operation:apply", …)`; there is no general re-broadcast. Prior row: MOD-D-42.
edit: No board change. Constraint for FIG-D-11's fonts work and FIG-D-21's templates work: do not draw a state whose only trigger is a FONT_* or TEMPLATE_* event, because those events cannot reach any subscriber the chrome can register.
